newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel sharply higher vs dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel sharply higher vs dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose sharply against the dollar and basket of key foreign currencies on Thursday and dealers said that the Bank of Israel will soon have to intervene once more in the forex market.

"The session opened with low activity and the market was quiet," said Gideon Sadeh at Bank Leumi. "By midday the business sector started converting foreign currency into shekels and the shekel rose sharply."
Sadeh said there was no evident reason for the currency conversions of the companies.

He added that the shekel was traded at only 0.5 percent below the higher edge of its trading band. "The market expects that the central bank will be forced to start buying dollars soon, maybe even next week, to prevent the shekel from strengthening beyond its band," Sadeh said.

The Bank of Israel stopped intervening in the forex market in mid-June, after it slashed interest rates by 1.2 percentage points following a government decision to widen the currency's trading band and lower its crawling slope.
Sadeh added that in the near term the shekel is expected to move in a range of 3.52 to 3.535 shekels per dollar.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5290 shekels compared with 3.5410 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.7414 against 3.7506 on Wednesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.9712 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.9683 on Wednesday, and against the mark at 1.8764 shekels compared with 1.8762 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.5300 shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
